TerrainDesc.village: Settlement. You can rest at an inn and restock IP.
TerrainDesc.city: Large settlement with shops and travel services.
TerrainDesc.camp: Protected area: a safe place to rest in the wilds.
TerrainDesc.sea: Needs a vessel. Allow passage on the card or the terrain.
TerrainDesc.ruins: Point of interest: remains of something old.
TerrainDesc.dungeon: Point of interest: a dungeon entrance.
TerrainDesc.capital: The heart of the kingdom: palace, councils, markets and every service.
TerrainDesc.ruralVillage: Farms, a mill and plain folk. A place to rest and restock.
TerrainDesc.portCity: Docks, ships and routes to faraway lands. A good place to book a crossing.
TerrainDesc.merchantCity: Fairs, caravans and moneychangers: everything is bought and sold.
TerrainDesc.undergroundCity: Streets carved into the rock, lit by crystals and forges.
TerrainDesc.floatingCity: Platforms and towers hovering over the water, held by chains and magic.
TerrainDesc.fishingVillage: Boats on the sand, nets drying in the sun and the smell of the tide.
TerrainDesc.tribalVillage: Huts, totems and a common fire. The elders know the paths.
TerrainDesc.industrialCity: Chimneys, furnaces and workshops that never sleep.
TerrainDesc.academicCity: Libraries, observatories and scholars on every corner.
TerrainDesc.holyCity: Temples, pilgrims and bells. Here, faith rules.
TerrainDesc.abandonedCity: Empty houses and doors banging in the wind. No one knows why everyone left.
TerrainDesc.nobleDistrict: Mansions, gardens and private guards. Visitors are watched.
TerrainDesc.slums: Narrow alleys, patched roofs and people who know everything.
TerrainDesc.ruinCity: A living city built on top of an ancient civilization.
TerrainDesc.walledVillage: Walls, gates and lookouts: the frontier protects itself as it can.
TerrainDesc.enchantedForest: Whispering trees and lights that guide or mislead.
TerrainDesc.darkForest: Closed canopy, little light and eyes among the branches.
TerrainDesc.fairyGrove: Flowery clearings, mushroom rings and laughter in the air.
TerrainDesc.vastPlains: Grass to the horizon under an endless sky.
TerrainDesc.flowerFields: Seas of flowers, bees and a fragrant wind.
TerrainDesc.poisonSwamp: Purple water, toxic mist and bursting bubbles.
TerrainDesc.oasis: Fresh water and palm shade in the middle of the desert.
TerrainDesc.snowyMountains: White peaks, cutting winds and avalanches.
TerrainDesc.canyon: Red rock walls and a river far below.
TerrainDesc.waterfalls: Falling water, wet rocks and rainbows in the mist.
TerrainDesc.crystalLake: Water so clear the bottom shows. Something shines down there.
TerrainDesc.tropicalBeach: White sand, palm trees and warm sea.
TerrainDesc.isolatedIsland: A lonely piece of land in the sea. Only reachable by boat.
TerrainDesc.crystalCave: Huge crystals glowing in the dark. Valuable and dangerous.
TerrainDesc.dragonValley: Nests, giant bones and the shadows of wings in the sky.
TerrainDesc.dungeonWing: A stone hall with pillars. Echoes of steps that are not yours.
TerrainDesc.dungeonCell: Rusty bars, chains and marks on the wall.
TerrainDesc.dungeonCorridor: A torchlit corridor. Traps usually wait here.
TerrainDesc.abandonedMine: Rails, overturned carts and tunnels held up by rotten beams.
TerrainDesc.catacombs: Walls of bones and endless niches.
TerrainDesc.royalCrypt: The tomb of ancient kings, with treasures and guardians.
TerrainDesc.ancientRuins: Pyramids and inscriptions of a forgotten people.
TerrainDesc.forgottenTemple: A temple taken by the jungle. Its gods still listen.
TerrainDesc.wizardTower: A crooked tower full of books, experiments and locked doors.
TerrainDesc.monsterCastle: Torn banners and creatures on the battlements.
TerrainDesc.undergroundPrison: Lightless cells, cruel jailers and forgotten prisoners.
TerrainDesc.alchemyLab: Bubbling flasks, colorful smoke and the smell of sulfur.
TerrainDesc.forbiddenLibrary: Chained shelves and books that read their readers.
TerrainDesc.elementalShrine: An altar where fire, water, earth and air meet.
TerrainDesc.dimensionalDungeon: Rooms that move around and doors to other worlds.
TerrainDesc.derelictShip: A metal hull fallen from the sky. Lights still blink inside.
TerrainDesc.militaryFortress: Thick walls, cannons and a garrison on alert.
TerrainDesc.cursedGraveyard: Crooked tombstones, mist and the restless dead.
TerrainDesc.buriedCity: Towers and domes half buried in the sand.
TerrainDesc.fairyRealm: Castles of flowers and mushrooms. Promises here have weight.
TerrainDesc.astralPlane: A floor of starry mist and stone islands floating in the void.
TerrainDesc.dreamDimension: Impossible colors, stairs to nowhere and living memories.
TerrainDesc.petrifiedForest: Stone trees, crystal leaves and silence.
TerrainDesc.starSea: An ocean of night sky. A magical vessel is needed to cross it.
TerrainDesc.realmOfDead: Gray land, wandering souls and a river of no return.
TerrainDesc.colossalTree: A tree the size of a mountain, with towns on its branches.
TerrainDesc.celestialGarden: Flowers of light and golden fountains. A place of peace.
TerrainDesc.demonAbyss: A rift of fire and screams that goes down forever.
TerrainDesc.invertedWorld: Mountains hanging from the sky and rivers falling upward.
TerrainDesc.timeIsland: Stopped clocks and mixed eras. Time flows differently.
TerrainDesc.primordialCrystal: A gigantic crystal pulsing with the power of the world.
TerrainDesc.spiritSanctuary: Lanterns, wooden gates and spirits that guard those who rest.
TerrainDesc.dimensionPortal: A ring of runic stone with another world on the other side.
TerrainDesc.autoFactory: Conveyors, mechanical arms and machines that make machines.
TerrainDesc.steampunkCity: Gears, airships and steam rising from every roof.
TerrainDesc.trainStation: Rails, whistles and trains that shorten journeys.
TerrainDesc.researchLab: Screens, test tubes and scientists behind glass.
TerrainDesc.powerPlant: Turbines, contained lightning and a hum that never stops.
TerrainDesc.oilPlatform: A steel tower over the sea, with flames on top.
TerrainDesc.junkyard: Mountains of scrap, useful parts and forgotten robots.
TerrainDesc.spaceBase: Launch pads and antennas pointed at the stars.
TerrainDesc.planetColony: Glass domes under a strange sky with two moons.
TerrainDesc.magicWeaponsFacility: Mana crystals in war machines. Restricted access.
TerrainDesc.adventurersGuild: A quest board, bounties and tavern tales.
TerrainDesc.merchantsGuild: Contracts, scales and vaults. Business is made here.
TerrainDesc.magicAcademy: Starry towers, spell classes and curious students.
TerrainDesc.university: Study halls, a dome and scholars of every field.
TerrainDesc.barracks: Soldiers, drills and the command of the guard.
TerrainDesc.combatArena: Fights, bets and glory before the crowd.
TerrainDesc.colosseum: A giant amphitheater for tournaments and shows.
TerrainDesc.centralMarket: Stalls, cries and goods from all over the world.
TerrainDesc.inn: A warm bed, a meal and a safe place to sleep.
TerrainDesc.restaurant: Fine dishes and a famous kitchen.
TerrainDesc.casino: Dice, cards and fortunes changing hands.
TerrainDesc.museum: Relics, old maps and secrets on display.
TerrainDesc.thermalBaths: Hot water, steam and true rest.
TerrainDesc.religiousOrder: A cathedral, clerics and knights of the faith.
TerrainDesc.firstDungeon: A cave close to home. The first step of every journey.
TerrainDesc.waterDungeon: Flooded halls, currents and creatures of the deep.
TerrainDesc.earthDungeon: Roots, moving rocks and endless tunnels.
TerrainDesc.airDungeon: Platforms in the sky and winds that push toward the abyss.
TerrainDesc.iceDungeon: Frozen corridors, slippery floors and paralyzing cold.
TerrainDesc.poisonDungeon: Toxic gas, carnivorous plants and bubbling pools.
TerrainDesc.lightDungeon: Golden halls and trials for the pure of heart.
TerrainDesc.darkDungeon: Living darkness and shadows with a will of their own.
TerrainDesc.challengeTower: Floor after floor, each with a harder trial.
TerrainDesc.finalLabyrinth: Shifting walls and the last test before the end.
TerrainDesc.villainFortress: The great enemy's lair, ringed with flames and soldiers.
TerrainDesc.lastDungeon: Where everything ends. There is no way back.

rest.name: Rest
rest.desc:
The group rests for 4 to 6 hours. Each PC recovers all HP and MP and recovers from all status effects.
In the wilds you need a magic tent, someone's hospitality or a safe place; in settlements, an inn room or hospitality.
At the end of the rest scene, each PC may create a Bond, add an emotion to a Bond or swap an emotion. Immediate threats may advance while you rest.
rest.tentText: Created with 4 IP from a single character. Fits the whole group.
rest.hospText: Someone friendly takes the group in, usually for help or money.
rest.safeText: Somewhere with no risk of attack: a consecrated temple, a secret room, a magic circle...

item.name: Use an inventory item
item.desc: Spend IP from a single character to create the item in the backpack and use it right away. Nothing is kept for later.
item.tonicText: One creature recovers from all status effects.
item.shardText: 10 air, bolt, fire, earth or ice damage to one creature you can see.
item.tentText: Lets the group rest in the wilds.

restock.name: Restock IP
restock.desc: In villages, towns and other places with shops, each IP recovered costs 10 zenit. IP never exceeds the character's maximum and cannot be shared between characters.
restock.prompt: Who restocks, and how many IP?

services.name: Travel services
services.desc: Passage for one day of travel, per person. Price and availability depend on the world, and a vehicle may increase the distance of a travel day.

newPlace.name: New place on the map
newPlace.desc: Spend 1 Fabula Point to add an element to the story: a new place on the map (a village, a ruin, a shortcut...). Describe it; the GM decides how and where it appears.
newPlace.prompt: Describe the place the group finds:

explore.name: Scout the area
explore.desc: House rule: the group spends part of the day surveying the region and turns the cards up to 2 away. Counts as one card walked that day.

cartography.name: Cartography
cartography.desc: Camp activity (optional rule). Once before your next rest, after a group travel roll, roll again and keep the new result.

camp.name: Camp activity
camp.desc: Optional rule. In each rest scene, each PC performs one of the two activities they have and applies the benefit to the target. "Once" benefits last until the next rest.
camp.combatText: An ally: once, adds +4 to an Accuracy check or an offensive Magic check.
camp.magicText: An ally: once, casts a spell you know, paying its cost and making the checks.
camp.cartoText: You: once, reroll a group travel roll and keep the new result.
camp.harvestText: A gourmet: roll 1d6. 1: an easy conflict at the end of the rest; 2: 2 random ingredients; 3-5: 3 random; 6: 3 of your choice.
camp.owlText: You: generate 3 progress points for a project.
camp.daydreamText: You: once, when you lose HP, lose only half.
camp.exerciseText: You: once, avoid all status effects you would suffer from a single source.
camp.scoutText: You or an ally: roll 1d6. 1: you recover only half your HP and MP; 2: the target recovers 2 IP; 3-5: 3 IP; 6: 3 IP and you find 50 × your level in zenit.
camp.forgeText: You: repair a group item, create a basic weapon, armor or shield for free, or break equipment down into a material.
camp.massageText: An ally: once, pays half the MP cost (not for rituals).
camp.pepText: An ally: once, doubles the MP they recover.
camp.planText: An ally: once, +4 when leading a group check or examining something or someone.
camp.doubleText: An ally: once, doubles the HP they recover.
camp.sleepText: You: once, one extra action on your turn (Equipment, Hinder or Inventory).
camp.martialText: You: once, when attacking, gain multi (2) or +1 multi.

Sample.chest: An old chest caught between roots. Inside are 300 zenit and a torn map pointing north.
Sample.dungeon: The entrance of a forgotten dungeon, guarded by hollow-eyed statues.
Sample.ruins: Broken columns of a temple. Someone lit a fire here not long ago.

movePermission.name: Who moves the group
movePermission.hint: Players click an adjacent card (or use the arrow keys) and the connected GM validates the step.

flipSound.name: Card flip sound
flipSound.hint: Path of the audio file. Leave empty for no sound.

autoOpen.name: Open the map when the GM shows it
autoOpen.hint: Opens the map automatically when the GM clicks Show to players.

OutcomeHint.danger: The GM describes a danger. The group may avoid it with a group check, a series of checks or, rarely, a conflict.
OutcomeHint.discovery: The group makes an unexpected discovery. Discoveries are always good.
OutcomeHint.calm: Nothing special happens on this travel day.

Chat.treasureHunter: Treasure Hunter: discovery on {max} or less
Chat.dangerHow: A danger should be avoidable with a group check or a series of checks; it rarely becomes a conflict. Damage by group level (core p. 108):
Chat.dangerLocked: The group stays put until you release movement (lock on the map toolbar).
Chat.dayEndText: Threat of the day: {threat} ({die}). Roll the Travel Roll with the Roll button on the map.
Chat.dayEndPlayers: Threat of the day: {threat}. A player rolls the Travel Roll ({die}) with the Roll button on the map. The group travels on after the roll.

Status.rollNow: Roll the Travel Roll for day {day} ({die})
Status.gmWillRoll: Day {day}: the GM will roll the Travel Roll

Reason.queryFailed: The GM did not answer. Try again.
Reason.locked: The group is stopped by a danger. Wait for the GM to release it.
Reason.notAdjacent: Pick a card next to the group.
Reason.noParty: The group is not on the map.
Reason.gmOnlyMove: In this world only the GM moves the group.
Reason.notActive: That map is no longer active.
Reason.noRoll: There has been no Travel Roll yet.
Reason.gmOnlyOption: Only the GM can use that option.
Reason.error: Something went wrong. See the console (F12).
Reason.rollPending: The day's Travel Roll is missing. Roll it before travelling on.
Reason.noPending: There is no pending Travel Roll.
Reason.gmRolls: On this map, the GM rolls the Travel Roll.
Reason.badDie: That roll does not match the day's die.

Notify.queryFailed: The GM did not answer. Try again.
Notify.badMacro: No macro found for this option.
Notify.importFailed: Invalid file. Use a JSON exported by the Card Atlas.
Notify.shownPlayer: The GM showed a map. Open it with the map button in the token controls.
Notify.noActorImage: That actor has no token image.
Notify.newTerrains: Card Atlas: {count} new terrains were added to your library.

Empty.gm: No maps yet. Generate a new map or start from the sample map.
Empty.player: The GM has not shown a map yet.

Toolbar.peekOn: Seeing hidden cards. Click to see what players see.
Toolbar.peekOff: Seeing what players see. Click to see hidden cards.

Cell.title: Card ({x}, {y})
Cell.label: Name on the card
Cell.textHint: Posted to chat the first time the group arrives here.
Cell.linkHint: Drop a journal, scene or actor here

New.title: New map
New.name: Name
New.seedHint: The same code, theme and size always make the same map. Write down the code of a map you like.
New.sampleHint: A ready 16 × 10 map with a village, road, forest, river, sea, dungeon and treasure.
New.editHint: Once created, everything can be edited: paint terrain, rename cards, move the group.
New.startVillage: Found a village on the chosen card
New.startHint: Click a card in the preview to choose where the group starts.

ThemeDesc.continent: Land surrounded by sea, with mountains, forests, rivers and roads linking the villages to a city.
ThemeDesc.archipelago: Islands scattered across the sea. Sea routes link the ports: those sea cards can be crossed.
ThemeDesc.desert: Sand as far as the eye can see, oases, rocky ridges and more ruins than usual.
ThemeDesc.frozen: Frozen wastes, pine forests and a cold sea to the north. Few villages.
ThemeDesc.wilds: Dense woods, jungle to the south, swamps and many rivers. Few villages.
ThemeDesc.kingdom: A kingdom full of people: the capital with its noble district and slums, port, merchant, academic and holy cities, walled villages on the frontier and dungeons that fit the land.
ThemeDesc.wonders: Enchanted and dark forests, fairy groves, flower fields, canyons, waterfalls, crystal lakes, beaches, oases, crystal caves and the dragon valley.
ThemeDesc.journey: A world made for progression: the first dungeon near the start, the elemental dungeons midway, ice, poison, light and darkness farther away, and the tower of trials, the final labyrinth, the villain's fortress and the last dungeon at the end.
ThemeDesc.mystic: Magical planes linked by bridges over a sea of stars: the fairy realm, the dream dimension, the astral plane, the inverted world, the realm of the dead, a colossal tree, portals and the primordial crystal.
ThemeDesc.machines: A steampunk city, train stations, factories, power plants, labs, a military complex, a platform at sea, a junkyard, a cyberpunk city and, far away, the space base and a colony on another planet.
ThemeDesc.metropolis: A whole city in cards: avenues, noble districts and slums, the market, guilds, academy, university, barracks, arena, colosseum, taverns, inns, a restaurant, casino, theater, museum, thermal baths and the religious seat. The group starts at an inn.
ThemeDesc.dungeonCrawl: Rooms (wings), corridors and cells linked together, with solid rock around them (no card). The entrance is at the bottom; catacombs, a prison, a lab, a library, a shrine and, deepest of all, the royal crypt.

Gen.dungeon1: A staircase goes down into the dark. The air rising from it is cold and damp.
Gen.dungeon2: Iron gates stand ajar on a hillside. There are fresh claw marks in the dirt.
Gen.dungeon3: A tower sunk into the ground, only its top showing. A light flickers inside.
Gen.treasure1: A half-buried chest bearing the crest of a forgotten noble house.
Gen.treasure2: A smuggler's cache: bags of coins and a letter with instructions.
Gen.treasure3: An ancient offering on a stone altar. No one has touched it in centuries.
Gen.ruins1: The fallen walls of a fortress. Someone camped here not long ago.
Gen.ruins2: Faceless statues ring an empty square. The wind carries a distant song.
Gen.ruins3: A temple split in two. Its inscriptions speak of a seal and a key.

Confirm.delete: Delete the map "{name}"? This cannot be undone.
Confirm.hideAll: Turn every card face down? Cards around the group stay face up.
Confirm.resetTravel: Go back to day 1 and clear the trail and the last roll?

Config.title: Configure map
Config.name: Name
Config.sizeHint: Growing adds plains cards; shrinking deletes the cards that no longer fit.
Config.revealRadiusHint: After each step, turns the cards within this distance of the group (0 = only the card the group stands on).
Config.movesPerDayHint: How many cards the group walks in one travel day. The roll uses the highest threat among the day's cards.
Config.lockOnDangerHint: On a danger, the group only walks again when the GM releases it.
Config.tablesHint: Optional. Drop a table from the sidebar; it is drawn on a danger or a discovery.
Config.wayfarerHint: Tick what some PC has (core p. 176-177).
Config.veteran: Well-Traveled (die one size smaller, minimum d6)
Config.treasureHunter: Treasure Hunter (discovery on SL + 1 or less)
Config.practical: Resourceful (reminder: recover SL IP after each roll)
Config.rollBy_auto: Automatic, at the end of each day
Config.rollByHint: With the GM or the players, a Roll button appears in the map's status line at the end of the day, and the group only travels on after the roll. The GM can always roll.
Config.lookfarHint: Opens the Lookfar module's Travel Check with the day's die already chosen. Lookfar's roll counts for the map, and Lookfar generates the danger or discovery. Use with The GM or The players in Who rolls.
Config.lookfarMissing: The Lookfar module is not active in this world. With this option on, the map keeps using its own Travel Roll.
Config.actorDrop: Drag an actor here to use its token
Config.partyFrameHint: No frame shows the image as it is, good for tokens with a transparent background.
Config.partyLabelHint: Optional, for example the group's name
Config.manaChatHint: The first time the group reaches a card with visible mana, the mana message is posted in the chat.
Config.manaMessageHint: Used for every mana card. Write {element} for the element's name and {place} for the card's name. Leave blank for the default sentence. Below, each element can have its own sentence; each card can have its own in the card panel.

Terrains.title: Terrain library
Terrains.intro: Each terrain sets the image, the threat level (the Travel Roll die) and whether it can be crossed. "Name banner" writes the name on the card, as for cities and points of interest.
Terrains.name: Name
Terrains.resetConfirm: Replace the library with the default terrains? Cards of deleted terrains lose their image.

Options.title: Travel options
Options.intro: Cards the players hold while travelling. "Announce in chat" only posts the card; "Travel Roll", "Reroll" and "Turn cards" (value = radius) are run by the GM; "Run macro" runs the macro whose UUID is in the value. "Spends a card of the day" counts as one card walked. Choices: one per line, as Name | cost | effect.
Options.name: Name
Options.step: Spends a card of the day
Options.choices: Choices: Name | cost | effect (one per line)
Options.resetConfirm: Replace every option with the defaults?

Mana.title: Latent mana
Mana.hidden: Only the GM sees the mana
Mana.messageHint: Blank uses the board's message (Board settings). {element} and {place} work here.
Mana.chatOff: Mana chat messages are turned off in Board settings.
